title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a 'Résumé' begun on p.48. For a smooth projective variety T of dimension n over an algebraically closed field k, there are two abelian varieties built from cycles algebraically equivalent to zero: A_T = Alb(T), built from 0-cycles, and B_T = Pic^0(T)_red, the 'Picard généralisé', built from divisors. A correspondence Z on X×Y of suitable dimension induces a homomorphism between A or B of X and A or B of Y. There are 4 = 2×2 cases. Grothendieck asserts three things: the map depends only on the numerical class of Z; with Q-coefficients every homomorphism of abelian varieties arises this way; and the statement can be translated into ℓ-adic cohomology.

The translation uses two canonical identifications:
(i) H^1(A_T,Q_ℓ) ≅ H^1(T,Q_ℓ), via pull-back along the Albanese map.
(ii) H^1(B_T,Q_ℓ) ≅ H^{2n-1}(T,Q_ℓ)(n-1). This comes from V_ℓ Pic^0 = H^1(T,Q_ℓ(1)) by Kummer theory, followed by dualising and Poincaré duality: H^1(T)(1)^∨ = H^{2n-1}(T)(n)(-1).
Through these identifications, the maps on H^1 / H^{2n-1}(n-1) induced by Q-homomorphisms of abelian varieties are exactly those induced by Q-algebraic cycles on X×Y.

Consequence: suppose a cycle-induced map between the relevant 'H^1-type' groups of X and Y is an isomorphism. Then it corresponds to an isogeny A→B. The inverse isogeny exists in Hom⊗Q, so it is again induced by a Q-cycle. Hence the inverse of the cohomological isomorphism is algebraic.

Announced application: take X of dimension n and ample classes ξ_1,…,ξ_{n-1}. Then cup product by ξ_1⋯ξ_{n-1}, H^1(X)→H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1), is induced by the diagonal cycle cut by the ξ_i. It corresponds to the classical isogeny Alb(X)→Pic^0(X), or its dual, obtained through a complete-intersection curve. So its inverse is induced by an algebraic Q-correspondence. This is the Lefschetz standard conjecture B(X) (or A) in degree 1, in a 'mixed' form with possibly distinct ample classes.

The next page tabulates the four cases with their commutative squares. Case III (Alb_X → Pic_Y) is the classical theory of divisorial correspondences and needs no denominators. Cases I, II and IV require inverting φ or ψ, which is done via hard Lefschetz in degree 1 and introduces denominators.
errors: The second identification is first written as H^{2n-1}(B_T,Q_ℓ); in the image the exponent seems overwritten with '1'. The correct statement is H^1(B_T,Q_ℓ) ≅ H^{2n-1}(T,Q_ℓ)(n-1), as on the next page (ψ: H^{2m-1}(Y)(m-1)→H^1(B_Y)).

Minor: in positive characteristic B_T must be taken as the reduced Pic^0. Also, 'depends only on numerical class' is asserted without argument here. On H^1-type Künneth components homological and numerical equivalence agree, so it is correct, but it uses the degree-1 Lefschetz/Weil theory.

ideas.what: Identification of H^1 of the Albanese and of the Picard variety with H^1(T) and H^{2n-1}(T)(n-1)
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-adic realization of the Albanese/Picard 1-motives (h^1 and h^{2n-1} of a motive)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969); Kleiman 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Q-homomorphisms of Albanese/Picard varieties correspond exactly to Q-correspondences on X×Y (four cases)
ideas.modern_name: Theory of divisorial correspondences; Hom(Alb_X, Pic_Y)⊗Q = cycles in H^1⊗H^1 part

ideas.what: Inverse of hard Lefschetz H^1→H^{2n-1}(n-1) (by ξ_1⋯ξ_{n-1}, ξ_i ample) is induced by an algebraic Q-cycle
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture B(X) in degree 1 (mixed ample classes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck / Kleiman (degree-1 case of standard conjecture B)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck 1969 Bombay paper remarks the degree-1 case follows from Picard/Albanese theory; Kleiman 1968, 1994

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known proof of the Lefschetz standard conjecture in degree 1 via Albanese/Picard isogenies, later published by Grothendieck (1969) and Kleiman (1968). Using several distinct ample classes ξ_1,…,ξ_{n-1} is a minor variation that is classical in degree 1. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Second line of the displayed system: read H^1(B_T,Q_ℓ) ⟸ H^{2n-1}(T,Q_ℓ)(n-1); the exponent on B_T appears corrected to 1 in the manuscript.

'De plus, la bonne correspondance entre formes de cl. cohomologiques' is likely 'De plus, la bijection [correspondance] entre homom. de cl. cohomologiques relatifs à X et à Y'. The sense: isomorphisms on the H^1-type groups correspond to isogenies A→B.
Struck word '[-correspondante-]' followed by 'une isog.'. The intended phrase is roughly 'correspond à une isogénie A→B et une isogénie' (i.e. the inverse is also an isogeny).
